identificationModule.briefTitle: ICI-VPH: Impact of HPV Immunisation Schedules Against HPV
identificationModule.officialTitle: ICI-VPH: Impact Des Calendriers d'Immunisation Contre Les HPV

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
This randomised clinical trial aims to determine whether an immunization schedule comprising two doses of Gardasil administered six months apart is non-inferior to a schedule comprising three doses administered at 0, 6 and 60 months for the prevention of HPV-16 and HPV-18 infections that persist for at least six months, up to ten years after the initial vaccination.

The study hypothesis is that the two-dose schedule would offer similar protection as that of a three-dose schedule against persistent HPV-16/18 infections.

armGroups.label: 2 dose of quadrivalent HPV vaccine
armGroups.description: The participants who have already received 2 doses of the quadrivalent HPV vaccine (0, 6 months schedule) 5 years before recruitment will not receive an additional dose.

armGroups.label: 3 doses of quadrivalent HPV vaccine
armGroups.description: The participants will receive a 3rd dose of quadrivalent HPV vaccine at recruitment visit, which is 5 years after having received two doses of vaccine given 6 months apart in grade 4 (0, 6, 60 months Schedule)

interventions.name: Quadrivalent HPV vaccine
interventions.description: One dose of Gardasil administered in the intervention group

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Geometric mean titres of antibodies and seropositivity for HPV types 6, 11, 16 and 18

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Having received two doses of Gardasil in 2008-2009, 2009-2010,2010-2011 or 2011-2012 according to 0, 6 months Schedule (between 4 and 12 months)
* Resident of the regions chosen for the study

Exclusion Criteria:

* Being considered immunosuppressed at time of vaccination (9-10 years-old) or at recruitment visit
* Being pregnant at recruitment visit
